title: The AI feature that matters way more than benchmark
description:
Everyone's obsessed with which AI model scored higher on the latest benchmark. But the thing that actually changed how I use these tools is browser control — letting the agent open a browser and read the real page instead of answering from memory.

When an AI answers from memory, it'll confidently make things up: the wrong version of the docs, a setting that doesn't exist, an answer that was true a year ago. When it can go read the real page, it stops guessing. That's the line between when agents are useful and when they'll burn you.

So next time an AI gives you a super confident answer, ask yourself: did it actually go look, or is it just going off memory? If it didn't look, don't fully trust it.

For builders, founders, and creators who want the few AI things that actually matter — minus the hype.
